[USER] User expressed interest in CERN's collaboration with other institutions.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] CERN collaborates with universities and research institutions worldwide in high-energy physics, involving over 120 participating institutions in the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) experiments.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] CERN collaborates with other institutions in nuclear physics, with the Isotope Separator On-Line Radioactive Ion Beam Facility (ISOLDE) as a prominent example.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] CERN researchers work with other institutions in astrophysics to study cosmic rays, dark matter, and other phenomena beyond our solar system.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] CERN's technology is used in medical physics research, specifically in developing proton therapy for cancer treatment.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Proton therapy uses high-energy protons that can be precisely targeted to cancerous tissue while sparing surrounding healthy tissue.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] CERN's technology generates proton beams using a particle accelerator, with the Proton Synchrotron (PS) being the world's first dedicated proton accelerator.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] CERN collaborates with medical physicists and physicians to develop and refine proton therapy treatment techniques and conduct research on the biological effects of proton radiation on cancer cells.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Particle accelerators have many applications, including:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Materials Science: Used for ion implantation to create and study new materials.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Radioisotope Production: Produces short-lived isotopes for medical imaging and cancer treatment.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Security Inspection: Used in airport security scanners to identify hidden explosives and dangerous materials.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Environmental Science: Analyzes environmental samples to study pollution and contaminants.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Aerospace: Simulates the effects of space radiation on electronics.
